_: EP 19 — Blue-green deployment, in depth. The STATION STRIP construction (references/station-strip.md) wearing the FERRARI EDITORIAL surface (references/ferrari-editorial.md) — near-black #181818 canvas that is never pure black, Rosso Corsa #da291c used scarcely, SHARP 0px corners on every surface (the opposite of EP13–18, all built on 12–20px radii), Inter 500 at -1% tracking as the documented FerrariSans substitute, display weight never bold, elevation by brightness step (#181818 → #303030) plus a 1px hairline and NO drop shadows. The act break is the system's own `livery-band` — a full-width Rosso Corsa band — instead of the white chapter slate EP16–18 use; three of them in the film is the entire red budget. Five Kling plates carry the depth the system demands: cold open, title, two subjectless ambient textures run under the graphics acts, and the end card. No morph bridges this episode. EVERY FIGURE IS SOURCED OR FRAMED AS ONE SYSTEM'S: blue-green is Humble and Farley, Continuous Delivery (2010), after Daniel Terhorst-North; expand/contract is Fowler and Sato's ParallelChange (2014); AWS ALB deregistration delay defaults to 300 seconds; Kubernetes terminationGracePeriodSeconds defaults to 30 seconds; a load balancer target-group swap moves traffic in seconds while DNS does not, because resolvers and client runtimes cache past the TTL. The per-system numbers on screen — a 2-hour window, 11,400 in-flight requests, a 4-minute bake, 2x infrastructure for 18 minutes — are labelled as this system's measurements, not industry facts.
title: Nothing Ships At
subtitle: Blue-green deployment: build the new stack beside the old one, then move the traffic.
hook: The maintenance window was never necessary.
next: Next: canary releases, and the one percent that tells you everything
_theme: New palette: `ferrari`, straight out of the supplied design extract. The series continuity is the CONSTRUCTION, the voice and the cue set — never the colour. This is the darkest film in the playlist and the only one with sharp corners.
_voice: Unchanged from EP 13–18 — same voice id, same model, same settings. Every line opens on an instruction verb.
_music: Same 84bpm grid as EP 13–18 so scene lengths snap identically across the run.
_vo: Eleven lines, three acts. Act one builds the second stack; act two moves the traffic and then makes you wait; act three is what it costs, ending on the database — the part of blue-green that is neither blue nor green and the reason the pattern is harder than the diagram.

vo.text: Price the maintenance window. Two hours of downtime at two in the morning, and an engineer awake to watch it.
Build the second stack first. Two identical environments. One takes traffic, one waits.
Own the switch point. A load balancer flips in seconds. DNS keeps handing out the old answer.
Deploy into the idle one. Green takes the new build and warms its caches, touching nobody.
Test the thing you will ship. Green runs on real infrastructure… against real dependencies.
Now move the traffic. One target group swap, and every new request lands on green instead of blue.
Let the old stack finish. Requests already in flight on blue still need somewhere to land.
Watch three numbers. Error rate, tail latency, saturation. Four minutes of it, not forty seconds.
Keep blue running. Rollback is a switch you already own, not a deploy you have to build.
Now the hard part… The database is shared, so it is NEVER blue and never green.
Then pay for it. Two full environments at once, and state that belongs to neither.

_shots: Five plates. The Ferrari system is explicit that full-bleed cinematic photography IS the depth treatment and that drop-shadow tiers are not used, so this is the first episode in the run where footage is a design requirement rather than a flourish. Subject is dark data-hall photography and subjectless macro texture — never cars, because borrowing a design register is fair and generating footage that reads as another company's marketing is not.
